record.paper_title: Infinity in string cosmology: A review through open problems
record.original_question: If the scalar field and fluid are allowed to interact in Robertson-Walker braneworld models derived from gravi-dilaton string effective actions or their Einstein-frame versions, can those interactions generate regular asymptotics and simultaneously satisfy the three constraints inherited from the previous brane problem?

evidence.quote:
4.3 RW branes with interactions
This project will search the question as to whether regular asymptotics are the result of the interactions between the scalar ﬁeld and the ﬂuid. It would be interesting to test whether interacting ﬂuids can meet all three conditions discussed in the previous problem.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a Robertson–Walker braneworld cosmological model derived from a gravi-dilaton string effective action (or its Einstein-frame counterpart). On the brane, assume the matter content consists of (i) a scalar field φ with potential V(φ) and (ii) a perfect cosmological fluid with energy density ρ and pressure p = wρ, together with a covariant interaction term Q describing energy–momentum exchange between φ and the fluid, so that the conservation equations take the form

   ρ̇_φ + 3H(ρ_φ + p_φ) = −Q,    ρ̇ + 3H(ρ + p) = Q,

with ρ_φ = ½φ̇² + V(φ), p_φ = ½φ̇² − V(φ), and H = ȧ/a the Hubble rate of the brane scale factor a(t). The modified Friedmann equation on the brane reads

   H² = (κ²/3)(ρ_φ + ρ) + (1/36)(ρ_φ + ρ)² + Λ/3 + 𝓔/a⁴ ± k/a²,

where κ², Λ, and the dark-radiation term 𝓔/a⁴ arise from the bulk and brane tensions.

Determine whether there exists a choice of V(φ), of the fluid equation-of-state parameter w, and of the interaction current Q such that:

(a) every solution (a(t), φ(t), ρ(t)) is geodesically complete and free of curvature singularities for all t ∈ ℝ (regular past and future asymptotics);

(b) the following three constraints are simultaneously satisfied:
   (1) the weak energy condition for the total cosmic fluid holds along the entire evolution;
   (2) the model admits a viable late-time accelerated expansion phase (effective dark-energy regime) consistent with H > 0 and ä > 0 at late times;
   (3) the early-time asymptotic regime matches a bounded, non-singular configuration of the gravi-dilaton string effective action (e.g. a pre-big-bang-type fixed point or a regular bounce).

In other words: can interactions between the scalar field and the fluid produce regular asymptotics while meeting the three conditions above?
artifact.status_search_result: No specific resolution of this interacting Robertson–Walker brane problem (regular asymptotics together with the three stated constraints) was located in the literature. While there is extensive work on interacting dark-energy/dark-matter braneworld models and on non-singular pre-big-bang cosmologies, none directly confirm a solution meeting all three conditions in the gravi-dilaton brane setting. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Interacting dark energy in braneworld cosmology
status_evidence.snippet: Studies of scalar field–fluid interactions on the brane discuss late-time acceleration but do not address regular global asymptotics with energy-condition constraints.
status_evidence.claim: Related work treats interacting components on the brane without resolving the regularity-plus-constraints question.
